name: Clown Motel
note: Famously billed 'America's Scariest Motel' — clown-themed rooms next to the historic Tonopah cemetery. The iconic must-stop oddity of the route.

name: Mizpah Hotel
note: 1907 silver-boom grande dame, restored by the Cline family in 2011; member of Historic Hotels of America. Reputedly haunted by the 'Lady in Red.'

name: Tonopah Brewing Company
note: Local craft brewery and BBQ spot; the Mizpah even sells a brewery package with beer coupons. Best craft beer for miles.

name: Tonopah Liquor Company
note: Family-owned bar in a 1907 building — atmospheric old-Nevada watering hole downtown.

name: Jack Dempsey Room
note: Bar/restaurant inside the Mizpah named for the boxer, who once worked here as a bouncer/saloon man.

name: Happy Burro Chili & Beer
note: Beatty's most famous spot — award-winning chili verde, chili burgers, ice-cold beer, western patio. A genuine desert institution.

name: Sourdough Saloon
note: Laid-back western bar with dollar bills covering the walls and ceiling; burgers, cocktails, and gateway-to-Death-Valley character.

name: Mel's Diner
note: Voted 'Best Dive in Nevada'; known for chicken fried steak. Classic roadside diner energy.

name: Exchange Club Motel
note: Pet-friendly motel built in 1906 — a long-running historic stop on the edge of Death Valley.

name: Mad Greek Cafe
note: Eye-catching blue-and-white Greek roadside cafe famous for gyros and date shakes; featured on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives. The Baker landmark eatery.

name: Alien Fresh Jerky
note: UFO-themed roadside shop with a 'crashed' flying saucer facade and hundreds of jerky flavors. Pure desert kitsch on I-15.

name: International Cafe & Bar
note: Genuinely Nevadan bar inside a building built in Virginia City in 1859 and moved to Austin in 1863 — said to be the oldest structure in Nevada. Burgers and Indian tacos.

name: Pony Canyon Motel
note: Budget-friendly motel on Highway 50 'the Loneliest Road'; clean rooms with A/C, fridge, free parking.

name: Cellblock Steakhouse
note: Ely's only fine dining, set in a former jail — you can dine inside an actual barred cell. Best cuts of meat in White Pine County.

name: Jailhouse Motel & Casino
note: Jail-themed motel/casino in historic downtown Ely; home to the Cellblock Steakhouse and Smash N Grab burgers.

name: Hotel Nevada & Gambling Hall
note: Historic 1929 hotel-casino, once the tallest building in Nevada; downtown Ely landmark with vintage neon.

name: Juanita y Chava
note: Authentic Mexican — street tacos, burritos, and a well-loved salsa bar. Local favorite.

name: Erick Schat's Bakkery
note: Eastern Sierra landmark since 1938, famous for its original Sheepherder Bread. The essential Bishop pilgrimage stop.

name: Mountain Rambler Brewery
note: Downtown brewpub with handcrafted beers and New American food; favorite of climbers and hikers off Highway 395.

name: Holy Smoke Texas Style BBQ
note: Dry-rubbed brisket and Texas-style smoked meats; a strong Bishop BBQ pick.

name: WayFinder Bishop
note: Boutique downtown inn on Bishop Creek — design-forward base for Eastern Sierra adventures.

name: Alabama Hills Cafe & Bakery
note: #1-ranked Lone Pine restaurant; hearty breakfast/lunch with daily fresh-baked breads. Named for the nearby movie-backdrop Alabama Hills.

name: Mt. Whitney Restaurant
note: Family spot at Highway 395 & Whitney Portal Rd serving the best burgers in town — beef, buffalo, or elk. Three meals a day.

name: Dow Villa Motel
note: Historic 1923 motel-and-hotel that hosted Hollywood Western stars (John Wayne et al.) shooting in the Alabama Hills.

name: Rocking V Cafe
note: Kanab's best-regarded restaurant — art-filled slow-food eatery in an 1892 mercantile building; meats to vegan. Open daily.

name: Vermillion 45
note: Casual bistro with French, Belgian and Italian dishes plus fresh seafood and steaks. Top date-night/gourmet pick in Kanab.

name: Parry Lodge
note: Historic 1931 motor lodge on the National Register; hosted golden-age Hollywood stars. Heated pool, on-site dining, Old Barn Theater.

name: Best Friends Roadhouse and Mercantile
note: Pet-centric inn tied to the famous Best Friends Animal Sanctuary; unusually welcoming to road-trippers traveling with animals.

name: Milt's Stop & Eat
note: Beloved Moab landmark since 1954 — classic burgers, fries, and hand-spun shakes from a vintage roadside stand.

name: Moab Brewery
note: Moab's original microbrewery (since 1996); home of Dead Horse Ale. Big family-friendly menu after red-rock adventures.

name: Desert Bistro
note: Casual-upscale bistro in a historic building — elk tenderloin, bacon-wrapped dates. Reservations recommended in peak season.

name: Sorrel River Ranch
note: Riverfront ranch resort on Highway 128 along the Colorado River outside town; with on-site dining and dramatic canyon setting.

name: Stone Hearth Grille
note: Scratch-made all-natural dining with hilltop Bryce Canyon views; seasonal (spring through fall). Best fine-ish dining near Bryce.

name: IDK Barbecue
note: Small-town smoked-meats joint near Bryce Canyon with a cult following for its brisket and sauce.

name: Stone Canyon Inn
note: Started as a 2000 B&B, now cabins, bungalows and treehouses just outside Bryce Canyon — a standout boutique stay.

name: Bryce Canyon Coffee Company
note: Local coffee, hot chocolate and fresh baked goods — the morning stop before sunrise at the hoodoos.

name: Cruiser's Cafe 66
note: 1930s filling-station-turned-cafe in downtown Williams with restored gas pumps, smoked BBQ, full bar and patio. Quintessential Route 66.

name: Pine Country Restaurant
note: Williams comfort-food institution famous for its homemade pies. At 107 N Grand Canyon Blvd.

name: Grand Canyon Railway Hotel
note: 298-room hotel beside the 1908 depot where the Grand Canyon Railway departs; Spenser's Pub has an 1800s bar. AAA 3-diamond.

name: Elote Cafe
note: Sedona's most celebrated restaurant — chef Jeff Smedstad's Mexican/Southwestern; the namesake elote and smoked-brisket enchiladas. Reservations essential.

name: Mariposa Latin Inspired Grill
note: Upscale South-American-inspired grill with floor-to-ceiling red-rock views; spectacular at sunset. Resort-casual dress code, reservations required.

name: Coffee Pot Restaurant
note: Sedona breakfast institution beneath Coffee Pot Rock — famous for '101 omelettes.'

name: L'Auberge de Sedona
note: Luxury creekside resort on Oak Creek with an acclaimed on-site restaurant; one of Sedona's signature stays.

name: Pizzicletta
note: Tiny beloved pizzeria with wood-fired Neapolitan pies cooked in ~90 seconds; you can take the pizza next door to Mother Road.

name: Mother Road Brewing Company
note: Flagstaff Route 66 brewery at 7 S. Mikes Pike; relaxed taproom, often paired with Pizzicletta pies.

name: Diablo Burger
note: Creative burgers on branded English muffins using 100% local grass-fed beef; a downtown Flagstaff favorite committed to regional sourcing.

name: Tinderbox Kitchen
note: Upscale dinner-only comfort food (buffalo meatloaf, juniper-cured venison); the adjacent Annex is a more casual lounge.

name: CasaBlanca Resort & Casino
note: 450+ room tower with 24-hour casino, championship golf, spa, and Katherine's fine dining. Mesquite's flagship resort.

name: Eureka Casino Resort
note: Employee-owned Mesquite casino resort known for friendly service and lavish suites with jetted tubs.

name: Gregory's Mesquite Grill
note: Steaks and Italian fare; a go-to sit-down dinner option in Mesquite.

name: Primm Valley Resort & Casino
note: State-line I-15 casino-hotel at the NV/CA border; as of June 2026 Terrible's signed to operate the Primm properties, keeping this desert outpost alive.

name: Buffalo Bill's Resort & Casino
note: Home of the Desperado roller coaster on the state line. Note: shuttered as a full-time destination in 2025 — a haunting, half-empty landmark, perfect road-trip lore.

name: Painted Pony
note: Fine dining in Ancestor Square — modern American with a Southwestern twist and locally sourced ingredients. St. George's top special-occasion table.

name: Xetava Gardens Cafe
note: Calming patio cafe in the Kayenta Art Village surrounded by red rock; brunch, lunch, dinner — gyro salad and Mahi tacos.

name: Inn at Entrada
note: Premier St. George resort with luxury casitas, fireplaces, jetted tubs and private patios beneath the red cliffs.

name: El Capitan Lodge & Casino
note: Hawthorne's main casino-hotel, anchoring this Army-depot town on Walker Lake; the El Capitan Diner serves burgers and all-day breakfast.

name: Maggie's Restaurant
note: Local Hawthorne sit-down restaurant at 785 E St — one of the town's few but valued dining spots.

name: Bruno's Country Club & Motel
note: Founded 1952 by Italian immigrant Bruno Selmi on the edge of the Black Rock Desert (Burning Man's playa) — a 50-room motel, cafe and bar/casino in one. Famous meat-filled ravioli. The only real stop in Gerlach.
